title: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.15640v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Streaming video understanding aims to continuously process incoming visual observations, making the retention and retrieval of relevant information increasingly important as the video history grows. Although existing benchmarks include memory-related questions, question-answering accuracy alone does not reliably measure memory capabilities. Incorrect predictions may arise from failures in visual understanding rather than forgetting, whereas correct predictions may rely on linguistic priors or recent observations without requiring historical memory. To address these ambiguities, we introduce MemInStream, a benchmark dedicated to evaluating memory capabilities in streaming video understanding. We develop an evidence-controlled validation protocol that associates each question with temporally localized evidence intervals. translated_title: MemInStream：是记忆还是仅仅识别？重新思考流式视频记忆评估
translated_abstract: 流式视频理解旨在持续处理不断传入的视觉观察，随着视频历史的增长，相关信息的保留与检索变得日益重要。尽管现有基准包含了与记忆相关的问题，但仅凭问答准确率并不能可靠地衡量记忆能力。错误的预测可能源于视觉理解能力的不足而非遗忘，而正确的预测可能依赖于语言先验或近期观察，无需借助历史记忆。为解决这些模糊性，我们提出了MemInStream，一个专门用于评估流式视频理解中记忆能力的基准。我们开发了一种证据控制的验证协议，将每个问题与时间上定位的证据区间相关联。该协议通过保留那些模型能够从相应证据区间解答、但必须依赖历史记忆才能回答的问题，来验证证据可解性与记忆必要性。
tldr: 该论文提出MemInStream基准及证据控制的验证协议，通过将问题与时间定位的证据区间关联，区分模型的真实记忆能力与语言先验或近期观察带来的假象，从而更可靠地评估流式视频理解中的记忆能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MemInStream, a benchmark with an evidence-controlled validation protocol that links each question to temporally localized evidence intervals, enabling reliable evaluation of memory capabilities in streaming video understanding by distinguishing genuine memory from linguistic priors or recency effects.
